name: detection and defence industry
reason: Detection is covered where a product or a rule set exists to name. The decisive questions, which are what each control can see, how long it retains it and whether anyone responds, are named by artefacts and never tested. This is the lens where the repo knows the vocabulary and not the behaviour.

L15-003.note: Decoding layers before matching is exactly what payload padding defeats, with a passed payload as the oracle.

L15-009.note: Body size handling at the edge is the factor and the technique.

L15-013.note: Defeating automation signals is the tool's stated purpose, with a treated-as-human request as the oracle.

L15-014.note: Solving a JavaScript challenge without an engine is the factor answered directly.

L15-053.note: Measuring detection coverage against a scoring test set is the independent check on a vendor claim.

L15-001.note: Placement of one payload across path, header, body and multipart is the inspection depth test.

L15-004.note: A structurally invalid request with no banned substring measures whether rules express structure.

L15-005.note: Traceability of every firing rule to a substring is the signature versus behaviour question.

L15-021.note: Host and server coverage per technique, with gaps named, is the telemetry listing.

L15-024.note: East west coverage is one of the listed telemetry gaps.

L15-027.note: Rule coverage per technique is the same measured matrix.

L15-046.note: Purple team validation is the entry's whole subject.

L15-062.note: Living off the platform is a named technique class with no local test.

L15-007.note: A position that is never inspected is functionally an exclusion list, and the test finds it.

L15-010.note: Multipart is one of the positions the test uses.

L15-026.note: A connection that bypasses the proxy is the factor, tested by attempting one.

L15-030.note: Which sources exist is the matrix.

L15-031.note: Ordering across sensors with measured drift is the clock question.

L15-032.note: Retention against the investigation window is a column in the matrix.

L15-033.note: Outbound channel coverage is tested by attempting each channel.

L15-048.note: A permission change with an actor and source address is the control plane log test.

L15-049.note: Sign-in events appearing centrally is the identity log export test.

L15-057.note: Whether a single operator can use the inspection key alone is the factor.

L15-064.note: Time from decision to enforced block, measured on a real action.

L15-002.note: Plaintext versus ciphertext is the first row of the matrix: a marker in the body either arrives readable or does not.

L15-006.note: A learning mode residue shows as a marker accepted that a tuned rule would block.

L15-008.note: A rule disabled after an incident shows as a position with no blocking at all.

L15-011.note: Whether the runtime agent fires is exactly the untested detection question.

L15-012.note: Downgraded from L2: Tamper resistance of an agent is not the renderer sandbox audit. The concept is named and no procedure for it is stated.

L15-015.note: Downgraded from L2: The body and content type limit entry is about inspection stops, not behavioural modelling of pointer and keystroke timing. The concept is named and no procedure for it is stated.

L15-016.note: Fingerprint stability is tested by changing one property at a time, which is the same bisection.

L15-017.note: Address class handling appears as a position where the marker is blocked for one source and not another.

L15-018.note: Rate limiting granularity is found by bisecting the property that resets the count.

L15-019.note: Account takeover signals are rows in the matrix: which anomaly is challenged and which passes.

L15-020.note: Distributed stuffing is pacing across addresses, which the limiter granularity test names.

L15-022.note: Command line completeness is a column in the telemetry matrix.

L15-023.note: Script block logging is the same column for interpreted code.

L15-025.note: DNS logging and retention are columns in the matrix.

L15-028.note: Detection latency is measured by timestamping the action and the alert.

L15-034.note: Zero trust policy evaluation is an approval and attribution question, which is what the privileged access trail answers.

L15-035.note: Device posture asserted versus measured is exactly the enrollment record test.

L15-036.note: Conditional access gaps are access that survives a policy, which the offboarding review finds.

L15-037.note: Administrative plane protection is the same privileged session audit.

L15-038.note: Downgraded from L2: The telemetry matrix entry does not cover decoy placement. The concept is named and no procedure for it is stated.

L15-039.note: Downgraded from L2: Deception consistency is not a column the matrix defines. The concept is named and no procedure for it is stated.

L15-040.note: Whether a planted token fires is a detection test, and the never-fired record is the oracle.

L15-042.note: A capture started within the stated window, hashed, with volatility order respected.

L15-044.note: Backup isolation is the key separability question: can a production credential delete the copy.

L15-045.note: Downgraded from L2: Restore duration is not measured by the matrix. The concept is named and no procedure for it is stated.

L15-047.note: Detecting only what the deployed product emits is the signature bias question.

L15-054.note: Defence in depth shows as the same marker blocked at two layers or only one.

L15-055.note: A default that disables a feature shows as a position with no blocking.

L15-056.note: A security product's own update channel is a supplier with publish authority, which is the maintainer trust test.

L15-058.note: Break glass bypassing its own controls is the approval trail question.

L15-059.note: The measured rate rather than a pass or fail is the effectiveness question.

L15-063.note: A hop with no owner is a column with no data.

L15-043.note: Downgraded from L2: Containment cost is a business decision. The capture entry tests whether a capture can happen inside a window, not what isolation costs.
